transcript: For the love of God, next time you move to a new city, do not forget the science-backed rule of proximity. I know it sounds ridiculous, but most people move somewhere new and they wait to meet people organically and they end up alone eight months later and wonder why nothing's clicking. But there's actually a science-backed way to make friends as an adult. It's got nothing to do with your personality, your alma mater, or how cool you are. I know it sounds insane. People don't become best friends with somebody that they share common interests with. They actually become friends with them after multiple times of seeing them in the same place and having continuous interaction showing that repeated unplanned contact with people actually leads to closer relationship meaning you can naturally manufacture seeing the same people consistently by going to the same places over and over again aka the gym the same coffee shops grocery stores you get the gist the first one's gonna feel awkward but a few months in you're gonna be the man around town that everybody knows trust
